findings.issue: Confirmation now means only that the ROOT process is gone. On POSIX, when the root has already been reaped, _kill's os.getpgid(proc.pid) raises, killed becomes False, _gone() reads True and tear_down returns True without ever signalling the session group. Any descendant the root left in its own session (start_new_session makes pgid == root pid, and the group outlives its leader) is neither killed nor accounted for, yet the caller records 'confirmed'. Before the diff the same path returned False (unconfirmed). The task description asked for exactly this root-only rule, so this is a narrowing of the claim 'the tree is stopped', not a departure from the ask; the module docstring and the teardown field's name still promise the whole tree. No case covers a root that exited leaving a live descendant.
findings.resolution: On POSIX, when getpgid fails for a reaped root, try os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGTERM/SIGKILL) (a session leader's pgid is its pid) and treat ProcessLookupError there as the proof the group is empty; keep 'confirmed' only on that. Add a case: root exits at once leaving a sleeping grandchild, kill command stubbed to fail, expect False or a killed grandchild. If the root-only rule is intended on Windows alone, say so in tear_down's docstring.
